newsitem.title: UK: Wray group wins landslide vote to take over Forest.
newsitem.headline: Wray group wins landslide vote to take over Forest.

text.p: A consortium led by property developer Nigel Wray was given the go-ahead to take over English Premier League soccer club Nottingham Forest on Monday after an overwhelming vote in favour by shareholders.

The 19-million-pound bid from Wray's Bridgford consortium was accepted at an extraordinary general meeting by 189 votes with only seven against, according to Larry Lloyd, a former Forest star and now a sports media personality.
"I'm absolutely delighted," Lloyd, a shareholder himself, told Reuters by phone after the meeting. "It was the only choice we could make to try to save this club."
Bridgford includes Wray, chairman of property group Burford and owner of Saracens rugby union club, author Phil Soar and former Tottenham Hostpur chairman Irving Scholar.

The consortium plans to pump 16 million pounds into the club to strengthen a squad battling against relegation. Some three million pounds will be available to shareholders who wish to take the cash and the consortium will inherit debts estimated at around seven million pounds.
The group plans to float the club and is anxious for it to maintain its premier league status. It is currently languishing third from bottom of the division.

Wray's group was the only bidder left in the battle for Forest by Monday after a consortium led by U.S. journalist Albert Scardino was forced out of the reckoning by the withdrawal of its main backer, Mercury Asset Management.
"We had to withdraw yesterday. Mercury scored an own goal," Scardino said.

Scardino said Mercury had told him on Friday evening that they had changed their view on the prospects for soccer clubs over the next two years or so. He said there had earlier been "no hint or suggestion" of the change of heart.
Scardino's attempts to resurrect the bid with the help of his two other backers, Electra Investment Trust and Nash Sells, failed to come to fruition this weekend.
